claim: Let \(G\) be a finite connected simple graph with \(n\) vertices, \(m\) edges, minimum degree at least \(2\), and girth at least \(5\). Then the Lovász neighborhood complex \(\mathcal N(G)\) simplicially collapses to a graph. If \(G\) is non-bipartite, then \(\mathcal N(G)\simeq \bigvee^{2m-2n+1}S^1\). If \(G\) is bipartite, then \(\mathcal N(G)\) has exactly two connected components and each is homotopy equivalent to \(\bigvee^{m-n+1}S^1\).

correctness.rationale: The proof identifies the maximal neighborhood simplices, proves pairwise intersections have size at most one from the girth condition, gives an explicit elementary-collapse order reducing each simplex relative to its vertices to a star, and counts the resulting graph exactly. Component structure is the even-walk equivalence relation, yielding one component in the non-bipartite case and the two bipartition classes otherwise. The finite checker independently replays the collapse on six representative graphs.

value.rationale: The statement is an all-parameter structural classification for a canonical topological graph functor. It removes any degree upper bound in the high-girth regime and converts the entire homotopy type to the elementary graph counts \(n\) and \(m\), while simultaneously covering regular, irregular, bipartite, and non-bipartite families. This is broader than a finite census or a single-design specialization.
